diagnostic.encoding: taskkill writes GBK and capture.mjs appends the bytes to a string as UTF-8, so cleanupProof.diagnostics is lossy. Both messages above were confirmed by encoding them as GBK and comparing after the same lossy decoding: equal for a 255 run and a 128 run.

e2e.mechanism: The worker gets deadline Date.now() + timeoutMs and the parent's stop timer uses the same timeoutMs, so both fire at about 150 ms. In all 240 runs the worker had already exited, or exited while taskkill /PID <worker> /T /F was walking its tree. services/runner/src/screenshot/capture.mjs accepts only exit 128 (with closed-browser evidence or the launch barrier not crossed) as already closed; the in-walk exit gives 255, so cleanupConfirmed is false. The check fails closed: it reports unconfirmed cleanup, never a false success.
